scenarios.name: Silent-fallthrough-in-loop: try/except inside for-loop with success-path fallthrough
scenarios.description: Based on Alpha4Gate Phase 4.5 pattern -- a for-loop wraps expensive_op(item) in try/except that only logs the exception; the catch block has no continue or re-raise, so save_checkpoint(result) below the try runs with stale or undefined result. 682 unit tests miss this; a 4-minute smoke test catches it.
scenarios.context: Diff adds src/alpha4gate/curriculum.py::iterate_curriculum(items) with: for item in items: try: result = expensive_op(item) except Exception: log.exception('crashed'); # falls through; save_checkpoint(result); advance_curriculum(result). Tests in tests/test_curriculum.py mock expensive_op to always succeed. --prompt: 'add curriculum iteration loop'. --reviewers code.

scenarios.name: Silent-fallthrough-in-hot-path: try/except inside a function called per-RL-step
scenarios.description: Based on the Alpha4Gate Phase D.6 case surfaced by the review-deep v1 M1 smoke (2026-05-22). The hot-path function train_step() wraps its core work in try/except that only logs the exception and returns normally; the per-RL-step caller has no signal that a step silently failed and proceeds to advance the curriculum and write a checkpoint against stale state. Distinct from silent-fallthrough-in-loop because the try/except is inside a helper function, not in a literal loop body -- the loop lives in the caller.
scenarios.context: Diff adds src/alpha4gate/training/step.py::train_step(state) -> StepResult with: try: result = run_ppo_update(state); return StepResult(ok=True, ...) except Exception: log.exception('train step crashed'); return StepResult(ok=False, ...). The caller in src/alpha4gate/training/loop.py does `for episode in episodes: result = train_step(state); state = advance(result); save_checkpoint(state)` and never branches on result.ok. Unit tests in tests/test_step.py call train_step once with a known-good state and assert result.ok is True; the exception path is never exercised. --prompt: 'add resilient train_step wrapper for the PPO loop'. --reviewers code.

scenarios.name: Plan-conformance lens parses Alpha4Gate table-format plan (Step D.6)
scenarios.description: Plan-conformance lens is given a --plan-step pointing at the real Alpha4Gate phase-d-build-plan.md which uses table-format (markdown table with step-id in the first column) rather than heading-format. The lens MUST detect the table-format, parse the D.6 row's columns, AND additionally read the surrounding narrative section in the same file (Phase D plans put the per-step table at the top of section 3.1 and the per-step details in narrative paragraphs earlier in the document near the touched-files list). Legacy v1 behavior silently skipped this lens when no ### Step heading was found; v2's table-format support replaces the silent skip with active parsing.
scenarios.context: Diff modifies bots/current/learning/rewards.py + bots/current/data/hyperparams.json to land Alpha4Gate Phase D Step D.6 (Backwards-compat: `use_build_order_reward` flag). --plan-step Alpha4Gate/documentation/plans/phase-d-build-plan.md:D.6. The plan file's section 3.1 contains the table row `| D.6  | #169  | code | Backwards-compat: \`use_build_order_reward\` flag |` AND earlier narrative paragraphs document the touched-file context: rewards.py loads rules via load_rules() and accumulates episode_total (RewardCalculator); hyperparams.json gains new keys `use_build_order_reward` (bool, default false) + `build_order_reward_alpha` (float, default 1.0). The lens combines the table row's columns with the narrative prose into a single ground-truth payload and grades the diff against it. --prompt: 'add backwards-compat use_build_order_reward flag per Alpha4Gate phase D.6'. --reviewers code. Expected: Plan-conformance lens emits PASS or NEEDS-WORK per the diff's actual conformance (test exercises only the table-format detection + parsing path); SKIPPED is NOT emitted (--plan-step was provided); NEEDS-CLARIFICATION is NOT emitted (the lens successfully located the step in table form at line 88 of the real plan file).

scenarios.name: Lint dedup: ruff F401 cite-by-reference demotes lens finding to FYI
scenarios.description: Synthetic Python diff that adds 'import os' at the top of src/foo.py without using os anywhere. The orchestrator ran scripts/lint_prepass.sh which wrote lint-findings.json containing a ruff F401 'unused import' finding at src/foo.py:12. The Bugs lens, reading the linter pre-pass per the Bugs lens § 'Linter pre-pass results' pre-section, would normally re-derive the same defect; per the cite-by-reference instruction the lens MUST instead emit an FYI-severity finding with rationale prefixed 'Already-flagged by ruff F401 — surfacing for awareness only.' If the lens slips and emits a Nit at src/foo.py:12 anyway, aggregator rule 7's lint-dedup path catches the escapee: it demotes the lens finding to FYI with rationale prefixed 'Cited-by-linter: ruff F401' and annotates also_flagged_by_linter={tool: ruff, rule: F401} for audit-trail completeness. The lint finding itself is NOT republished by the aggregator (it's already in lint-findings.json).
scenarios.context: Diff adds src/foo.py with `import os\n\ndef greet(name): return f'hello, {name}'`. tests/test_foo.py exercises greet(). lint-findings.json contains {tool: 'ruff', rule: 'F401', file_line: 'src/foo.py:12', message: "'os' imported but unused"}. Bugs lens emits a finding at file_line='src/foo.py:12' with severity Nit and rationale 'unused import os adds noise and can mask future genuine usage' (or, per cite-by-reference, an FYI with 'Already-flagged by ruff F401 — surfacing for awareness only.'). Expected: aggregator rule 7 lint-dedup demotes the Nit (if emitted) to FYI with rationale prefixed 'Cited-by-linter: ruff F401' AND adds also_flagged_by_linter={tool: 'ruff', rule: 'F401'} to the finding dict. --prompt: 'add greet helper'. --reviewers code. --lint-findings .review-deep/lint-findings.json.

scenarios.name: Absence-of-thing finding deduplicates across Correctness + Test quality lenses
scenarios.description: Synthetic diff that adds a new service entry point without a corresponding integration test. Both the Correctness lens AND the Test quality lens surface findings about the same absent integration test -- file_line is an absence (no anchor line in the diff for either finding), so per rule 7 the aggregator detects the duplicate by (anti_pattern, finding-summary fuzzy-match) and demotes all-but-one to FYI. Neither finding carries an anti_pattern tag, so primary-lens selection falls back to lens-spawn order (Correctness, Bugs, Test quality, Style, Plan-conformance); Correctness emits first and wins as primary. Test quality's emission demotes to FYI. Result: aggregated_verdict counts the finding once at its original severity, not twice.
scenarios.context: Diff adds src/toybox/services/notification.py::send_notification(user_id, channel, body) -- a new service entry point that fans out to email/SMS/in-app handlers. Diff also adds tests/test_notification.py with unit tests that mock each handler individually. No integration test exercises send_notification end-to-end through the real handler chain. Correctness lens flags 'the prompt claims fan-out is wired but no integration test verifies end-to-end behavior; correctness cannot be confirmed against intent' at Nit (file_line: 'tests/integration/ has no test_notification.py'; no anti_pattern). Test quality lens flags 'missing integration test for notification fan-out path; this is a critical-behavior coverage gap' at Nit (file_line: 'no test file for src/toybox/services/notification.py exists'; no anti_pattern). --prompt: 'add notification fan-out service'. --reviewers code. Expected: rule 7 detects the duplicate via finding-summary fuzzy-match on the 'missing integration test' shape; both findings have no anti_pattern so lens-spawn order wins; Correctness keeps the Nit (primary), Test quality demotes to FYI. aggregated_verdict has 1 Nit + 1 FYI instead of 2 Nits.

scenarios.name: End-to-end aggregator: 6-lens verdict directory through aggregate.py to sidecar + markdown
scenarios.description: Validates the v3 CLI-invocation + filesystem-IO contract for the extracted aggregator (per-rule logic is covered by aggregate.py --unit-test in-process; this scenario covers the script entrypoint, --lens-dir / --output-dir argparse, on-disk JSON read, on-disk sidecar write, and stdout markdown emission). A synthetic 6-lens verdict directory feeds scripts/aggregate.py; the resulting sidecar + stdout markdown are validated against an expected snapshot (timestamps + run-ids are placeholders; schema + rule outputs + markdown structure are the snapshot). Catches CLI-surface regressions that would slip past --unit-test (which calls aggregate() in-process without exercising the argparse / file-IO path).
scenarios.context: Synthetic inputs: 6 lens JSON files in a temp dir AND a synthetic lint-findings.json: (1) correctness.json -- overall_verdict='PASS', findings=[]; (2) bugs.json -- overall_verdict='NEEDS-WORK', findings=[{severity:'Block', anti_pattern:'silent-fallthrough-in-hot-path', file_line:'src/foo.py:42', rationale:'try/except in per-step helper swallows exception then returns; caller never branches on result.ok'}, {severity:'Nit', file_line:'src/foo.py:12', rationale:'import os never used'}]; (3) security.json -- overall_verdict='PASS', findings=[]; (4) test-quality.json -- overall_verdict='NEEDS-WORK', findings=[{severity:'Block', anti_pattern:'missing-integration-test', file_line:'tests/integration/ has no test_foo.py', rationale:'new module foo.py invoked from production but no integration test exercises the production caller end-to-end'}]; (5) style.json -- overall_verdict='PASS', findings=[]; (6) plan-conformance.json -- overall_verdict='SKIPPED', findings=[]. lint-findings.json: {tools_run:['ruff'], findings:[{tool:'ruff', rule:'F401', file_line:'src/foo.py:12', message:'unused import: os'}]}. Invocation: `python scripts/aggregate.py --lens-dir <dir> --output-dir <out> --skill-version v3`. Expected: sidecar at <out>/<timestamp>.json has top-level keys [timestamp, plan_step, skill_version, invocation, lens_verdicts, aggregated_verdict, model_tiers_used, deferred_uat_items]; skill_version='v3'; lens_verdicts is a 6-element array preserving spawn order (correctness, bugs, security, test-quality, style, plan-conformance); aggregated_verdict.result='NEEDS-WORK' (rule 1: severity dominance -- any Block on a non-skipped lens forces NEEDS-WORK); the bugs Nit at src/foo.py:12 demotes to FYI with rationale prefixed 'Cited-by-linter: ruff F401' (rule 7 lint-dedup, assertion 29); aggregated_verdict.rationale cites the 2 Block findings; stdout markdown renders a top-level NEEDS-WORK verdict line followed by per-lens sections with the Block findings surfaced first. --prompt: 'aggregate review-deep verdicts end-to-end'. --reviewers code.

scenarios.name: Security lens flags a secrets-file dump as Block, owned by Security (not Bugs)
scenarios.description: Based on .claude/rules/security.md § 'Never dump secret file contents' (void_furnace 2026-05-09 incidents). The diff adds an operator-debug script that cats a secrets-bearing file to stdout -- exactly the filter-defeating round-trip security.md forbids. This is the secret-dump failure mode (defect_class: secret-dump). The Security lens is the PRIMARY OWNER of this finding and MUST flag it Block; the Bugs lens, even if it notices, defers (Bugs = generic robustness, Security = security.md failure modes), so any Bugs co-flag at the same file_line demotes to FYI per aggregator rule 2's Security-primary routing (ANTI_PATTERN_PRIMARY['secret-dump'] == 'security'). The diff has no functional bug a generic Bugs/Correctness pass would catch -- the file is only reachable via the Security lens's security.md priming, which is the whole point of promoting Security out of Bugs.
scenarios.context: Diff adds scripts/debug_env.sh containing `echo '--- secrets ---'; cat /etc/void_furnace/secrets.env` (a stdout round-trip of a secrets-bearing file), plus a one-line README note 'run scripts/debug_env.sh to inspect the live secrets'. No other code changes; the script parses + runs fine, so Correctness/Bugs/Style/Test-quality have nothing block-class to say. --prompt: 'add an env-debug helper for operators'. No --plan-step supplied. --reviewers code. Expected: the Security lens emits 'Security verdict: NEEDS-WORK (1 Block, 0 Nit)' with a Block finding at scripts/debug_env.sh:<line of the cat>, defect_class secret-dump, reasoning citing security.md § 'Never dump secret file contents' and recommending a metadata-only check (stat / wc -c / file) or effect-based verification instead; the aggregated_verdict.result is NEEDS-WORK (rule 1 severity dominance: one Block forces NEEDS-WORK); the finding is owned by the Security lens (lens_id 'security'); if the Bugs lens also surfaces it at the same file_line, rule 2 demotes the Bugs copy to FYI because Security is the registered primary owner of security findings.
